  // pop: restore env, DEALLOCATE the callee frame, and wind scopeLoc back (LIFO allocation
  // makes the saved loc the callee frame's own loc). Sound because no closureVal outlives its
  // defining frame (frontend subset: no returned/stored closures; module defs live in loc 0).
  rule <k> #pop => V ~> CONT </k>
       <ret>   retV(V) => noRet </ret>
       <stack> ListItem(frame(CONT:K, CALLERL:Int, SAVEDL:Int)) => .List ... </stack>
       <env>   L:Int => CALLERL </env>
       <scopes> SC:Map => SC [ L <- undef ] </scopes>
       <scopeLoc> _ => SAVEDL </scopeLoc>
endmodule
// reference/src/semantics/call.k — MPY-CALL
// ONE call route for every callable: evaluate the callee to a VALUE (name lookup reaches
// builtins at the root; a cooled Attribute is a bound method), evaluate the args (the shared
// #evalArgs loop in core.k), then dispatch on the callee value:
//   closureVal    -> bind params, push a frame (user function)
//   boundMethodV  -> applyMethod
//   builtinV      -> the #iterNext folds (sum/all/any/max/min) or applyBuiltin
//   typeV         -> callable type objects: int(...) / str(...)

module MPY-CALL
  imports MPY-METHODS
  imports MPY-BUILTINS
  imports MPY-FUNCTIONS

  // a cooled attribute is a bound method value
  rule <k> Attribute(V:Val, M:String) => boundMethodV(V, M) ... </k>

  // evaluate callee, then args ([owise]: problem-local Call interceptions beat this)
  syntax KItem ::= #callee(Exprs)
  rule <k> Call(Fe:Expr, ARGS:Exprs) => Fe ~> #callee(ARGS) ... </k> [owise]
  rule <k> CV:Val ~> #callee(ARGS:Exprs) => #evalArgs(ARGS, .Vals, toCall(CV)) ... </k>

  // ==== dispatch on the callee value ========================================
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(OBJ:Val, M:String)), ACC:Vals) => applyMethod(OBJ, M, ACC) ... </k>

  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sum")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #sumAcc(OBJ, 0) ... </k>
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("all")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #allAcc(OBJ)    ... </k>
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("any")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #anyAcc(OBJ)    ... </k>
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("max")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #maxAcc0(OBJ)   ... </k>
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("min")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #minAcc0(OBJ)   ... </k>
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN:String)), ACC:Vals) => applyBuiltin(BN, ACC) ... </k> [owise]
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(typeV(T:String)),     ACC:Vals) => applyBuiltin(T, ACC)  ... </k>

  // ==== heap-object arguments/receivers =====================================
  // Builtins and type calls READ structure — deref the first two arg positions
  // (covers len/sum/all/any/max/min/sorted/list/set + zip's pair). Mutating list
  // methods take the ref itself; every other method receiver is deref'd.
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN:String)), (ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
        => #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN)), (V, REST)) ... </k>
       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
       [priority(40)]
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN:String)), (A:Val, ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
        => #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN)), (A, V, REST)) ... </k>
       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
       requires notBool isRefV(A)
       [priority(40)]
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(typeV(T:String)), (ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
        => #applyK(toCall(typeV(T)), (V, REST)) ... </k>
       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
       [priority(40)]

  syntax Bool ::= isMutMethod(String) [function, total]
  rule isMutMethod(M:String)
    => M ==String "append" orBool M ==String "sort" orBool M ==String "extend"
       orBool M ==String "insert" orBool M ==String "pop" orBool M ==String "remove"
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(ref(H:Int), M:String)), ACC:Vals)
        => #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(V, M)), ACC) ... </k>
       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
       requires notBool isMutMethod(M)
       [priority(40)]
  // non-mutating methods READ their heap-object arguments too (join's list);
  // mutators keep refs (append of a list into a list-of-lists stays aliased)
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(OBJ:Val, M:String)), (ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
        => #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(OBJ, M)), (V, REST)) ... </k>
       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
       requires notBool isMutMethod(M) andBool notBool isRefV(OBJ)
       [priority(40)]

  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(closureVal(PNS:ParamNames, BODY:Stmts, DEFL:Int)), ACC:Vals) ~> CONT
        => #bindP(PNS, ACC) ~> BODY ~> #endcall </k>
       <env>     CALLERL:Int => NEWL </env>
       <scopes>   STORE:Map => STORE [ NEWL <- scope(.Map, parent(DEFL)) ] </scopes>
       <scopeLoc> NEWL:Int => NEWL +Int 1 </scopeLoc>
       <stack>   .List => ListItem(frame(CONT, CALLERL, NEWL)) ... </stack>

  // annotated closure: the frame starts with the captured freevar cells, its
  // parent is the module scope (all enclosing-local reads go through cells),
  // and the cellvars' fresh cells allocate before params bind (a cellvar param
  // then writes through its cell in #bindP).
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(closureValC(PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames, BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)), ACC:Vals) ~> CONT
        => #allocCells(CVS) ~> #bindP(PNS, ACC) ~> BODY ~> #endcall </k>
       <env>     CALLERL:Int => NEWL </env>
       <scopes>   STORE:Map => STORE [ NEWL <- scope(CM [ "$cells" <- cellsMark(CVS) ], parent(0)) ] </scopes>
       <scopeLoc> NEWL:Int => NEWL +Int 1 </scopeLoc>
       <stack>   .List => ListItem(frame(CONT, CALLERL, NEWL)) ... </stack>

  syntax KItem ::= #allocCells(ParamNames)
  rule <k> #allocCells(.ParamNames) => .K ... </k>
  rule <k> #allocCells((CV:String, R:ParamNames)) => #allocCells(R) ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ CV <- cellRef(N) ], _) ... </scopes>
       <heap>    H:Map => (N |-> cellV(noneV)) H </heap>
       <heapLoc> N:Int => N +Int 1 </heapLoc>
       requires notBool N in_keys(H)
endmodule
// reference/src/semantics/builtins.k — MPY-BUILTINS

module MPY-BUILTINS
  imports MPY-CORE
  imports MPY-STR
  imports MPY-SET
  imports MPY-ITER
  imports MPY-RANGE
  imports MPY-INT
  imports MPY-METHODS

  // the builtins REGISTRY is core.k's builtinsScope (the -1 frame); names resolve by lookup

  // Call routing + argument evaluation live in call.k, which also routes the fold
  // builtins (sum/all/any/max/min) to the #_Acc folds below and everything else to
  // applyBuiltin. This module owns applyBuiltin + the fold implementations.
  syntax Val ::= applyBuiltin(String, Vals) [function]

  // ==== len(obj) — O(1) per kind ============================================
  syntax Int ::= seqLen(Val) [function]
  rule applyBuiltin("len", OBJ:Val, .Vals) => seqLen(OBJ)
  rule seqLen(list(VS:ValSeq))                  => vsLen(VS)
  rule seqLen(tuple(VS:ValSeq))                 => vsLen(VS)
  rule seqLen(str(IS:IntSeq))                   => isLen(IS)
  rule seqLen(setV(DS:IntSeq))                  => isLen(DS)
  rule seqLen(rangeObj(LO:Int, HI:Int, ST:Int)) => rangeLen(LO, HI, ST)

  // ==== list(seq) — materialize a list/tuple into a list (e.g. list(d.keys())) ==
  // Minimal: the "copy a sequence" case (list of a list is itself; list of a tuple keeps order).
  // list() of other iterables (str/range/set/zip) is added via the iterator fold when needed.
  // (k-cell — list() constructs a NEW object)
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("list")), (list(VS:ValSeq),  .Vals)) => #alloc(list(VS)) ... </k>
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("list")), (tuple(VS:ValSeq), .Vals)) => #alloc(list(VS)) ... </k>
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("list")), .Vals)                     => #alloc(list(.ValSeq)) ... </k>
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("list")), (str(CS:IntSeq), .Vals))   => #alloc(list(charsOf(CS))) ... </k>
  syntax ValSeq ::= charsOf(IntSeq) [function, total]
  rule charsOf(.IntSeq)                => .ValSeq
  rule charsOf(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq)) => vCons(str(iCons(C, .IntSeq)), charsOf(R))

  // ==== set(str) — distinct character codes =================================
  rule applyBuiltin("set", str(CS:IntSeq), .Vals) => setV(dedupCodes(CS))

  // ==== abs(int) ============================================================
  rule applyBuiltin("abs", I:Int, .Vals) => absInt(I)

  // ==== sum(iterable) — one #iterNext fold; intOf = int value of an int/bool ==
  syntax KItem ::= #sumAcc(Iterable, Int) | #sumCont(Int)
  rule <k> #sumAcc(IT:Iterable, ACC:Int) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #sumCont(ACC) ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #sumCont(ACC:Int) => ACC ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #sumCont(ACC:Int)
        => #sumAcc(R, ACC +Int intOf(V)) ... </k>
       requires isInt(V) orBool isBool(V)

  syntax Int ::= intOf(Val) [function]
  rule intOf(I:Int)  => I
  rule intOf(B:Bool) => #if B #then 1 #else 0 #fi

  // ==== all / any (short-circuiting #iterNext folds) ========================
  syntax KItem ::= #allAcc(Iterable) | "#allCont"
  rule <k> #allAcc(IT:Iterable) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #allCont ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #allCont => true ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #allCont => #allAcc(R) ... </k>
       requires truthy(V)
  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, _:Iterable) ~> #allCont => false ... </k>
       requires notBool truthy(V)

  syntax KItem ::= #anyAcc(Iterable) | "#anyCont"
  rule <k> #anyAcc(IT:Iterable) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #anyCont ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #anyCont => false ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, _:Iterable) ~> #anyCont => true ... </k>
       requires truthy(V)
  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #anyCont => #anyAcc(R) ... </k>
       requires notBool truthy(V)

  // ==== max / min over an iterable (#iterNext folds; first element seeds) ====
  syntax KItem ::= #maxAcc0(Iterable) | "#maxCont0" | #maxAcc(Iterable, Int) | #maxCont(Int)
  rule <k> #maxAcc0(IT:Iterable) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #maxCont0 ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #maxCont0 => #maxAcc(R, {V}:>Int) ... </k>
       requires isInt(V)
  rule <k> #maxAcc(IT:Iterable, M:Int) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #maxCont(M) ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #maxCont(M:Int) => M ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #maxCont(M:Int)
        => #maxAcc(R, maxInt(M, {V}:>Int)) ... </k>
       requires isInt(V)

  syntax KItem ::= #minAcc0(Iterable) | "#minCont0" | #minAcc(Iterable, Int) | #minCont(Int)
  rule <k> #minAcc0(IT:Iterable) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #minCont0 ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #minCont0 => #minAcc(R, {V}:>Int) ... </k>
       requires isInt(V)
  rule <k> #minAcc(IT:Iterable, M:Int) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #minCont(M) ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #minCont(M:Int) => M ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #minCont(M:Int)
        => #minAcc(R, minInt(M, {V}:>Int)) ... </k>
       requires isInt(V)

  // ==== variadic max / min (a Vals fold) ====================================
  syntax Int ::= maxVals(Int, Vals) [function]
  rule applyBuiltin("max", I:Int, REST:Vals) => maxVals(I, REST)
  rule maxVals(M:Int, .Vals)           => M
  rule maxVals(M:Int, (I:Int, R:Vals)) => maxVals(maxInt(M, I), R)

  syntax Int ::= minVals(Int, Vals) [function]
  rule applyBuiltin("min", I:Int, REST:Vals) => minVals(I, REST)
  rule minVals(M:Int, .Vals)           => M
  rule minVals(M:Int, (I:Int, R:Vals)) => minVals(minInt(M, I), R)

  // ==== bin(n) — "0b" + binary digit codes (promoted from 103's defined fold) ==
  rule applyBuiltin("bin", N:Int, .Vals) => str(iCons(48, iCons(98, binCodes(N))))
       requires N >=Int 0
  // negative operand: the '-' sign prefixes the magnitude's digits
  rule applyBuiltin("bin", N:Int, .Vals)
    => str(iCons(45, iCons(48, iCons(98, binCodes(0 -Int N)))))
       requires N <Int 0
  syntax IntSeq ::= binCodes(Int) [function, total]
  rule binCodes(0) => iCons(48, .IntSeq)
  rule binCodes(N:Int) => binAcc(N, .IntSeq) requires N >Int 0
  syntax IntSeq ::= binAcc(Int, IntSeq) [function, total]
  rule binAcc(0, ACC:IntSeq) => ACC
  rule binAcc(N:Int, ACC:IntSeq)
    => binAcc((N -Int pyMod(N, 2)) /Int 2, iCons(48 +Int pyMod(N, 2), ACC))
       requires N >Int 0

  // ==== enumerate(xs) — pairs (i, v); materialized eagerly over a list =========
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("enumerate")), (list(VS:ValSeq), .Vals))
        => #alloc(list(enumVS(VS, 0))) ... </k>
  syntax ValSeq ::= enumVS(ValSeq, Int) [function, total]
  rule enumVS(.ValSeq, _:Int) => .ValSeq
  rule enumVS(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq), I:Int)
    => vCons(tuple(vCons(I, vCons(V, .ValSeq))), enumVS(R, I +Int 1))

  // ==== map(str, xs) — eager (only the str case is in the subset) =============
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("map")), (typeV("str"), list(VS:ValSeq), .Vals))
        => #alloc(list(mapStrVS(VS))) ... </k>
  syntax ValSeq ::= mapStrVS(ValSeq) [function, total]
  rule mapStrVS(.ValSeq) => .ValSeq
  rule mapStrVS(vCons(I:Int, R:ValSeq)) => vCons(str(strToCodes(Int2String(I))), mapStrVS(R))
  rule mapStrVS(vCons(str(CS:IntSeq), R:ValSeq)) => vCons(str(CS), mapStrVS(R))

  // ==== int(x) identities (int(round(x)) composes through) ====================
  rule applyBuiltin("int", I:Int, .Vals) => I

  // ==== ord / chr ===========================================================
  rule applyBuiltin("ord", str(iCons(C:Int, .IntSeq)), .Vals) => C
  rule applyBuiltin("chr", I:Int, .Vals) => str(iCons(I, .IntSeq))
       requires 0 <=Int I andBool I <Int 128

  // ==== str(int) / str(str) =================================================
  rule applyBuiltin("str", I:Int, .Vals)       => str(strToCodes(Int2String(I)))
  rule applyBuiltin("str", str(CS:IntSeq), .Vals) => str(CS)

  // ==== int(str) — a single digit char ('0'..'9', code 48..57) to its value =====
  rule applyBuiltin("int", str(iCons(C:Int, .IntSeq)), .Vals) => C -Int 48
       requires 48 <=Int C andBool C <=Int 57

  // ==== int(str) — a multi-digit non-negative numeral (Horner fold; the single-char rule covers len 1)
  rule applyBuiltin("int", str(CS:IntSeq), .Vals) => intDigAcc(CS, 0)
       requires isLen(CS) >=Int 2
  syntax Int ::= intDigAcc(IntSeq, Int) [function, total]
  rule intDigAcc(.IntSeq, ACC:Int)             => ACC
  rule intDigAcc(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq), ACC:Int) => intDigAcc(R, (ACC *Int 10) +Int (C -Int 48))

  // ==== zip(a, b) — parallel iterable of pairs, truncating to the shorter =====
  rule applyBuiltin("zip", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq), .Vals) => zipObj(A, B)
  rule applyBuiltin("zip", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq), .Vals)   => zipObjS(A, B)

  // zip's iterator-protocol cases (zip is created here, so its #iterNext lives here)
  rule <k> #iterNext(zipObj(vCons(A:Val, As:ValSeq), vCons(B:Val, Bs:ValSeq)))
        => #iterYield(tuple(vCons(A, vCons(B, .ValSeq))), zipObj(As, Bs)) ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterNext(zipObj(.ValSeq, _:ValSeq))               => #iterDone ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterNext(zipObj(vCons(_:Val, _:ValSeq), .ValSeq)) => #iterDone ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterNext(zipObjS(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)))
        => #iterYield(tuple(vCons(str(iCons(A, .IntSeq)), vCons(str(iCons(B, .IntSeq)), .ValSeq))), zipObjS(As, Bs)) ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterNext(zipObjS(.IntSeq, _:IntSeq))              => #iterDone ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterNext(zipObjS(iCons(_:Int, _:IntSeq), .IntSeq)) => #iterDone ... </k>

  // ==== range(stop) / range(start, stop) / range(start, stop, step) =========
  rule applyBuiltin("range", I:Int, .Vals)               => rangeObj(0, I, 1)
  rule applyBuiltin("range", A:Int, B:Int, .Vals)        => rangeObj(A, B, 1)
  rule applyBuiltin("range", A:Int, B:Int, S:Int, .Vals) => rangeObj(A, B, S)
       requires S =/=Int 0

  // ==== eval(str) — arithmetic expressions (ints, + - * // **, spaces) ========
  // Python precedence: ** right-assoc, then * //, then + -. Promoted from 160's
  // trusted pass evaluator, now DEFINED in the reference and driven by a
  // code-level tokenizer. Reduces on concrete strings (krun); a symbolic
  // argument leaves the call unevaluated for problem-level folds.
  rule applyBuiltin("eval", str(CS:IntSeq), .Vals) => evalArith(CS)
  syntax Int ::= evalArith(IntSeq) [function]
  rule evalArith(CS:IntSeq)
    => firstNdE(passAddE(passMulE(passPowE(tokOps(CS), tokNds(CS)))))

  syntax OpSeq ::= ".OpSeq" | oCons(String, OpSeq)

  syntax Bool ::= evDigit(Int) [function, total]
  rule evDigit(C:Int) => C >=Int 48 andBool C <=Int 57
  syntax Bool ::= evHead42(IntSeq) [function, total]
  rule evHead42(iCons(42, _:IntSeq)) => true
  rule evHead42(_:IntSeq)            => false [owise]
  syntax Bool ::= evHead47(IntSeq) [function, total]
  rule evHead47(iCons(47, _:IntSeq)) => true
  rule evHead47(_:IntSeq)            => false [owise]

  syntax OpSeq ::= tokOps(IntSeq) [function, total]
  rule tokOps(.IntSeq)                 => .OpSeq
  rule tokOps(iCons(32, R:IntSeq))     => tokOps(R)
  rule tokOps(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq))  => tokOps(R) requires evDigit(C)
  rule tokOps(iCons(42, iCons(42, R:IntSeq))) => oCons("**", tokOps(R))
  rule tokOps(iCons(42, R:IntSeq))     => oCons("*", tokOps(R)) requires notBool evHead42(R)
  rule tokOps(iCons(47, iCons(47, R:IntSeq))) => oCons("//", tokOps(R))
  rule tokOps(iCons(47, R:IntSeq))     => oCons("/", tokOps(R)) requires notBool evHead47(R)
  rule tokOps(iCons(43, R:IntSeq))     => oCons("+", tokOps(R))
  rule tokOps(iCons(45, R:IntSeq))     => oCons("-", tokOps(R))

  syntax IntSeq ::= tokNds(IntSeq) [function, total]
                  | tokNdAcc(Int, IntSeq) [function, total]
  rule tokNds(.IntSeq)                => .IntSeq
  rule tokNds(iCons(32, R:IntSeq))    => tokNds(R)
  rule tokNds(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq)) => tokNdAcc(C -Int 48, R) requires evDigit(C)
  rule tokNds(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq)) => tokNds(R)
       requires notBool evDigit(C) andBool C =/=Int 32
  rule tokNdAcc(A:Int, iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq)) => tokNdAcc(A *Int 10 +Int (C -Int 48), R)
       requires evDigit(C)
  rule tokNdAcc(A:Int, S:IntSeq) => iCons(A, tokNds(S)) [owise]

  syntax EvPair ::= evp(OpSeq, IntSeq)
  syntax Int ::= firstNdE(EvPair) [function, total]
  rule firstNdE(evp(_:OpSeq, iCons(N:Int, _:IntSeq))) => N
  rule firstNdE(_:EvPair) => 0 [owise]

  syntax Int ::= applyOpE(String, Int, Int) [function, total]
  rule applyOpE("+",  A:Int, B:Int) => A +Int B
  rule applyOpE("-",  A:Int, B:Int) => A -Int B
  rule applyOpE("*",  A:Int, B:Int) => A *Int B
  rule applyOpE("//", A:Int, B:Int) => A divInt B
  rule applyOpE("**", A:Int, B:Int) => A ^Int B
  rule applyOpE(_:String, A:Int, _:Int) => A [owise]

  syntax EvPair ::= passPowE(OpSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
  rule passPowE(.OpSeq, NDS:IntSeq) => evp(.OpSeq, NDS)
  rule passPowE(oCons("**", OPS:OpSeq), iCons(N:Int, NDS:IntSeq)) => powCombE(N, passPowE(OPS, NDS))
  rule passPowE(oCons(O:String, OPS:OpSeq), iCons(N:Int, NDS:IntSeq)) => powCarryE(O, N, passPowE(OPS, NDS))
       requires O =/=String "**"
  rule passPowE(_:OpSeq, .IntSeq) => evp(.OpSeq, .IntSeq) [owise]
  syntax EvPair ::= powCombE(Int, EvPair) [function, total]
  rule powCombE(N:Int, evp(OPS:OpSeq, iCons(M:Int, REST:IntSeq))) => evp(OPS, iCons(N ^Int M, REST))
  rule powCombE(N:Int, evp(OPS:OpSeq, .IntSeq)) => evp(OPS, iCons(N, .IntSeq))
  syntax EvPair ::= powCarryE(String, Int, EvPair) [function, total]
  rule powCarryE(O:String, N:Int, evp(OPS:OpSeq, NDS:IntSeq)) => evp(oCons(O, OPS), iCons(N, NDS))

  syntax EvPair ::= passMulE(EvPair) [function, total] | passAddE(EvPair) [function, total]
  rule passMulE(evp(OPS:OpSeq, iCons(N0:Int, NDS:IntSeq))) => passLGoE("mul", N0, OPS, NDS, .OpSeq, .IntSeq)
  rule passMulE(evp(OPS:OpSeq, .IntSeq)) => evp(OPS, .IntSeq)
  rule passAddE(evp(OPS:OpSeq, iCons(N0:Int, NDS:IntSeq))) => passLGoE("add", N0, OPS, NDS, .OpSeq, .IntSeq)
  rule passAddE(evp(OPS:OpSeq, .IntSeq)) => evp(OPS, .IntSeq)
  syntax EvPair ::= passLGoE(String, Int, OpSeq, IntSeq, OpSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
  rule passLGoE(_:String, CUR:Int, .OpSeq, _:IntSeq, OO:OpSeq, ON:IntSeq) => evp(OO, appendIE(ON, CUR))
  rule passLGoE(L:String, CUR:Int, oCons(O:String, OPS:OpSeq), iCons(N:Int, NDS:IntSeq), OO:OpSeq, ON:IntSeq)
    => passLGoE(L, applyOpE(O, CUR, N), OPS, NDS, OO, ON)
       requires inLevelE(L, O)
  rule passLGoE(L:String, CUR:Int, oCons(O:String, OPS:OpSeq), iCons(N:Int, NDS:IntSeq), OO:OpSeq, ON:IntSeq)
    => passLGoE(L, N, OPS, NDS, appendOpE(OO, O), appendIE(ON, CUR))
       requires notBool inLevelE(L, O)

  syntax Bool ::= isIntV(Val) [function] | isStrV(Val) [function]
  rule isIntV(_:Int)         => true
  rule isIntV(_:Val)         => false [owise]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate an exhaustive declaration/rule inventory for the audited K sources."""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import re
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path


ROOTS = [
    Path("/reference/reference-semantics/semantics.k"),
    *sorted(Path("/reference/reference-semantics/semantics").glob("*.k")),
    Path("/candidate/verification.k"),
    Path("/candidate/spec.k"),
]
OUTPUT = Path("/audit-output/evidence/stage5-rule-inventory.tsv")
START = re.compile(
    r"^\s*(requires|module|endmodule|imports|configuration|syntax|rule|claim|context|alias)\b"
)


def records(path: Path) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
    lines = path.read_text().splitlines()
    starts: list[tuple[int, str]] = []
    for index, line in enumerate(lines):
        match = START.match(line)
        if match:
            starts.append((index, match.group(1)))
    out: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    for pos, (index, kind) in enumerate(starts):
        end = starts[pos + 1][0] if pos + 1 < len(starts) else len(lines)
        block_lines = lines[index:end]
        while block_lines and not block_lines[-1].strip():
            block_lines.pop()
        while block_lines and block_lines[-1].lstrip().startswith("//"):
            block_lines.pop()
        block = " ".join(part.strip() for part in block_lines if part.strip())
        attributes = sorted(set(re.findall(r"\[([^\]]+)\]", block)))
        flags = []
        for flag in [
            "function",
            "functional",
            "total",
            "symbol",
            "no-evaluators",
            "macro",
            "strict",
            "seqstrict",
            "priority",
            "owise",
            "simplification",
            "concrete",
            "anywhere",
        ]:
            if re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(flag)}\b", block):
                flags.append(flag)
        label_match = re.search(r"\[([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\]\s*:", block) if kind == "claim" else None
        out.append(
            {
                "file": str(path),
                "line": index + 1,
                "kind": kind,
                "claim_label": label_match.group(1) if label_match else "",
                "flags": ",".join(flags),
                "attributes": " | ".join(attributes),
                "text": block,
            }
        )
    return out


def main() -> int:
    all_records = [record for path in ROOTS for record in records(path)]
    with OUTPUT.open("w", newline="") as stream:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(
            stream,
            fieldnames=["file", "line", "kind", "claim_label", "flags", "attributes", "text"],
            dialect="excel-tab",
        )
        writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerows(all_records)

    kinds = Counter(record["kind"] for record in all_records)
    flags = Counter(
        flag
        for record in all_records
        for flag in str(record["flags"]).split(",")
        if flag
    )
    per_file = Counter(str(record["file"]) for record in all_records)
    print(f"files={len(ROOTS)}")
    print(f"records={len(all_records)}")
    print(f"kinds={dict(sorted(kinds.items()))}")
    print(f"flags={dict(sorted(flags.items()))}")
    for path in ROOTS:
        print(f"file_records[{path}]={per_file[str(path)]}")
    print(f"output={OUTPUT}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Compare selected satisfying-input theorem substitutions with both Python bodies."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import importlib.util
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+def load(name: str, path: str):
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path)
+    if spec is None or spec.loader is None:
+        raise RuntimeError(path)
+    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
+    return module
+
+
+def claimed_codes(strings: list[str]) -> list[int]:
+    # Ground instances use ASCII code sequences, exactly the K seqConcat fold.
+    codes: list[int] = []
+    for value in strings:
+        codes.extend(ord(char) for char in value)
+    return codes
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    canonical = load("canonical_witness", "/reference/canonical.py")
+    candidate = load("candidate_witness", "/candidate/solution.py")
+    cases = [[], ["q"], ["", "ab", "c"]]
+    rows = []
+    mismatch = False
+    for values in cases:
+        codes = claimed_codes(values)
+        claimed = "".join(chr(code) for code in codes)
+        canonical_value = canonical.concatenate(values)
+        candidate_value = candidate.concatenate(values)
+        ok = claimed == canonical_value == candidate_value
+        mismatch |= not ok
+        rows.append(
+            {
+                "input": values,
+                "k_claimed_codes": codes,
+                "k_claimed_string": claimed,
+                "canonical": canonical_value,
+                "candidate": candidate_value,
+                "all_equal": ok,
+            }
+        )
+    print(json.dumps({"witnesses": rows, "mismatch": mismatch}, indent=2))
+    return 1 if mismatch else 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

"""Compare selected satisfying-input theorem substitutions with both Python bodies."""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
import json
from pathlib import Path


def load(name: str, path: str):
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path)
    if spec is None or spec.loader is None:
        raise RuntimeError(path)
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module


def claimed_codes(strings: list[str]) -> list[int]:
    # Ground instances use ASCII code sequences, exactly the K seqConcat fold.
    codes: list[int] = []
    for value in strings:
        codes.extend(ord(char) for char in value)
    return codes


def main() -> int:
    canonical = load("canonical_witness", "/reference/canonical.py")
    candidate = load("candidate_witness", "/candidate/solution.py")
    cases = [[], ["q"], ["", "ab", "c"]]
    rows = []
    mismatch = False
    for values in cases:
        codes = claimed_codes(values)
        claimed = "".join(chr(code) for code in codes)
        canonical_value = canonical.concatenate(values)
        candidate_value = candidate.concatenate(values)
        ok = claimed == canonical_value == candidate_value
        mismatch |= not ok
        rows.append(
            {
                "input": values,
                "k_claimed_codes": codes,
                "k_claimed_string": claimed,
                "canonical": canonical_value,
                "candidate": candidate_value,
                "all_equal": ok,
            }
        )
    print(json.dumps({"witnesses": rows, "mismatch": mismatch}, indent=2))
    return 1 if mismatch else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

   165	                  [ "ord"    <- builtinV("ord")    ]
   166	                  [ "chr"    <- builtinV("chr")    ]
   167	                  [ "range"  <- builtinV("range")  ]
   168	                  [ "all"    <- builtinV("all")    ]
   169	                  [ "any"    <- builtinV("any")    ]
   170	                  [ "zip"    <- builtinV("zip")    ]
   171	                  [ "isinstance" <- builtinV("isinstance") ]
   172	                  [ "sorted" <- builtinV("sorted") ]
   173	                  [ "list"   <- builtinV("list")   ]
   174	                  [ "round"  <- builtinV("round")  ]
   175	                  [ "bin"    <- builtinV("bin")    ]
   176	                  [ "enumerate" <- builtinV("enumerate") ]
   177	                  [ "map"    <- builtinV("map")    ]
   178	                  [ "eval"   <- builtinV("eval")   ]
   179	                  [ "int"    <- typeV("int")       ]
   180	                  [ "str"    <- typeV("str")       ]
   181	                  [ "float"  <- typeV("float")     ], root)
   182	
   183	  // ==== argument/element evaluation: ONE left-to-right loop, tagged by destination ==
   184	  // (list/tuple literals and calls all use it; modules extend ApplyK with their tags)
   185	  syntax ApplyK ::= toCall(Val)
   186	  syntax KItem  ::= #evalArgs(Exprs, Vals, ApplyK)
   187	                  | #evalArgCont(Exprs, Vals, ApplyK)
   188	                  | #applyK(ApplyK, Vals)
   189	  rule <k> #evalArgs((A:Expr, REST:Exprs), ACC:Vals, K:ApplyK) => A ~> #evalArgCont(REST, ACC, K) ... </k>
   190	  rule <k> V:Val ~> #evalArgCont(REST:Exprs, ACC:Vals, K:ApplyK) => #evalArgs(REST, appendVal(ACC, V), K) ... </k>
   191	  rule <k> #evalArgs(.Exprs, ACC:Vals, K:ApplyK) => #applyK(K, ACC) ... </k>
   192	
   193	  // ==== Int / Bool / None literals ==========================================
   194	  rule <k> Int(I:Int)   => I ... </k>
   195	  rule <k> Bool(B:Bool) => B ... </k>
   196	  rule <k> NoneVal      => noneV ... </k>
   197	
   198	  // ==== truthy (If, Assert, BoolOp, IfExp, not, While) ======================
   199	  syntax Bool ::= truthy(Val) [function]
   200	  rule truthy(B:Bool)          => B
   201	  rule truthy(noneV)           => false
   202	  rule truthy(I:Int)           => I =/=Int 0
   203	  rule truthy(str(S:IntSeq))   => notBool (S ==K .IntSeq)
   204	  rule truthy(list(V:ValSeq))  => notBool (V ==K .ValSeq)
   205	  rule truthy(tuple(V:ValSeq)) => notBool (V ==K .ValSeq)
   206	
   207	  // ==== extensible operator dispatch (cases added by the construct modules) ==
   208	  syntax Val  ::= applyUn(String, Val) [function]
   209	  syntax Val  ::= applyBin(String, Val, Val) [function]
   210	  syntax Bool ::= applyCmp(String, Val, Val) [function]
   211	
   212	  // ==== shared list helpers =================================================
   213	  syntax Vals ::= appendVal(Vals, Val) [function, total]
   214	  rule appendVal(.Vals, V:Val)              => V , .Vals
   215	  rule appendVal((V0:Val, VS:Vals), V:Val)  => V0 , appendVal(VS, V)
   216	
   217	  syntax ValSeq ::= vals2valSeq(Vals) [function, total]
   218	  rule vals2valSeq(.Vals)            => .ValSeq
   219	  rule vals2valSeq((V:Val, VS:Vals)) => vCons(V, vals2valSeq(VS))
   220	
   221	  // ==== shared sequence length (len / summaries across many modules) ========
   222	  // (positional access valSeqAt/intSeqAt + normIdx live in subscript.k)
   223	  syntax Int ::= vsLen(ValSeq) [function, total]
   224	  rule vsLen(.ValSeq)                => 0
   225	  rule vsLen(vCons(_:Val, S:ValSeq)) => 1 +Int vsLen(S)
   226	
   227	  syntax Int ::= isLen(IntSeq) [function, total]
   228	  rule isLen(.IntSeq)                => 0
   229	  rule isLen(iCons(_:Int, S:IntSeq)) => 1 +Int isLen(S)
   230	
   231	  // in-bounds positional write (list subscript-assign); OOB leaves the seq unchanged
   232	  // (valid programs write in-bounds — mirrors valSeqAt's total-but-underspecified stance)
   233	  syntax ValSeq ::= setVSAt(ValSeq, Int, Val) [function, total]
   234	  rule setVSAt(.ValSeq, _:Int, _:Val)               => .ValSeq
   235	  rule setVSAt(vCons(_:Val, S:ValSeq), 0, V:Val)    => vCons(V, S)
   236	  rule setVSAt(vCons(W:Val, S:ValSeq), I:Int, V:Val) => vCons(W, setVSAt(S, I -Int 1, V))
   237	       requires I >Int 0
   238	  rule setVSAt(VS:ValSeq, I:Int, _:Val)             => VS
   239	       requires I <Int 0
   240	endmodule
     1	// reference/src/semantics/controls.k — MPY-CONTROLS

     3	module MPY-CONTROLS
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	  imports MPY-TUPLE
     6	  imports MPY-ITER
     7	
     8	  // ==== Assign / AugAssign (write the current scope; RHS evaluated by strictness) ==
     9	  rule <k> Assign(Name(X:String), V:Val) => .K ... </k>
    10	       <env> L:Int </env>
    11	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ X <- V ], _) ... </scopes>
    12	  rule <k> Assign(Name(X:String), V:Val) => #cellW({M[X]}:>Val, V) ... </k>
    13	       <env> L:Int </env>
    14	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    15	       requires "$cells" in_keys(M)
    16	        andBool pnMember(X, cellsOf({M["$cells"]}:>Val))
    17	        andBool X in_keys(M) andBool isCellRef({M[X]}:>Val)
    18	       [priority(40)]
    19	
    20	  rule <k> AugAssign(Name(X:String), OP:String, V:Val) => .K ... </k>
    21	       <env> L:Int </env>
    22	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ X <- applyBin(OP, {M[X]}:>Val, V) ], _) ... </scopes>
    23	       requires X in_keys(M)
    24	  // `lst += [..]` where lst is a heap ref: the generic rule leaves applyBin(OP, ref, V) — but the
    25	  // ref-deref preemption is BinOp-level (operators.k), so applyBin never derefs and it sticks. Route
    26	  // the ref case through BinOp so the deref + list-concat + #alloc path fires (result is a fresh ref).
    27	  rule <k> AugAssign(Name(X:String), OP:String, V:Val) => Assign(Name(X), BinOp(OP, Name(X), V)) ... </k>
    28	       <env> L:Int </env>
    29	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    30	       requires X in_keys(M) andBool isRefV({M[X]}:>Val)
    31	       [priority(40)]
    32	
    33	  // ==== import trivia: `from math import floor, ceil` binds the supported
    34	  // names as builtins in the current scope; every other import is a no-op
    35	  rule <k> ImportFrom("math", NS:ParamNames) => #bindImports(NS) ... </k>
    36	  rule <k> ImportFrom(_:String, _:ParamNames) => .K ... </k> [owise]
    37	  syntax KItem ::= #bindImports(ParamNames)
    38	  rule <k> #bindImports(.ParamNames) => .K ... </k>
    39	  rule <k> #bindImports((N:String, NS:ParamNames)) => #bindImports(NS) ... </k>
    40	       <env> L:Int </env>
    41	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ N <- builtinV(N) ], _) ... </scopes>
    42	       requires N ==String "floor" orBool N ==String "ceil"
    43	  rule <k> #bindImports((N:String, NS:ParamNames)) => #bindImports(NS) ... </k>
    44	       requires notBool (N ==String "floor" orBool N ==String "ceil")
    45	
    46	  // ==== Expr statement: evaluate for effect, discard the value ===============
    47	  // (bare calls — mutator methods, docstrings; the WP0 statement-trivia rung)
    48	  rule <k> Expr(_:Val) => .K ... </k>
    49	
    50	  // ==== If (condition evaluated by strictness) ==============================
    51	  syntax KItem ::= #branch(Bool, Stmts, Stmts)
    52	  rule <k> If(C:Val, T:Stmts, E:Stmts) => #branch(truthy(C), T, E) ... </k>
    53	  rule <k> #branch(true,  T:Stmts, _:Stmts) => T ... </k>
    54	  rule <k> #branch(false, _:Stmts, E:Stmts) => E ... </k>
    55	
    56	  // ==== IfExp: ternary T if C else E ========================================
    57	  rule <k> IfExp(V:Val, T:Expr, _:Expr) => T ... </k>
    58	       requires truthy(V)
    59	  rule <k> IfExp(V:Val, _:Expr, E:Expr) => E ... </k>
    60	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    61	
    62	  // ==== For: one loop, in-cell continuation, over #iterNext =================
    63	  // (the iterable is evaluated once, by strictness; the protocol stays rewrites —
    64	  // circularities anchor on #loop and narrowing substitutes the structure)
    65	  syntax KItem ::= #loop(Val, Expr, Stmts) | #loopStep(Expr, Stmts)
    66	                 | #while(Expr, Stmts) | #whileCond(Expr, Stmts)
    67	                 | #loopLbl(K) | "#cont" | "#brk"
    68	
    69	  rule <k> For(T:Expr, OBJ:Val, B:Stmts) => #loop(OBJ, T, B) ... </k>
    70	
    71	  rule <k> #loop(IT:Iterable, T:Expr, B:Stmts) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #loopStep(T, B) ... </k>
    72	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #loopStep(_:Expr, _:Stmts) => .K ... </k>
    73	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, REST:Iterable) ~> #loopStep(T:Expr, B:Stmts)
    74	        => #bindTgt(T, V) ~> B ~> #loopLbl(#loop(REST, T, B)) ... </k>
    75	
    76	  // ==== While ==============================================================
    77	  rule <k> While(C:Expr, B:Stmts) => #while(C, B) ... </k>
    78	  rule <k> #while(C:Expr, B:Stmts) => C ~> #whileCond(C, B) ... </k>
    79	  rule <k> V:Val ~> #whileCond(C:Expr, B:Stmts) => B ~> #loopLbl(#while(C, B)) ... </k>
    80	       requires truthy(V)
    81	  rule <k> V:Val ~> #whileCond(_C:Expr, _B:Stmts) => .K ... </k>
    82	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    83	
    84	  // ==== loop control (break / continue) =====================================
    85	  rule <k> #loopLbl(NEXT:K) => NEXT ... </k>
    86	  rule <k> Continue => #cont ... </k>
    87	  rule <k> Break => #brk ... </k>
    88	  rule <k> #cont ~> #loopLbl(NEXT:K) => NEXT ... </k>
    89	  rule <k> #cont ~> (_:KItem => .K) ... </k> [owise]
    90	  rule <k> #brk ~> #loopLbl(_:K) => .K ... </k>
    91	  rule <k> #brk ~> (_:KItem => .K) ... </k> [owise]
    92	
    93	  // ==== heap-object deref at the truthiness/iteration consumers ==============
    94	  // (priority(40) preempts the generic Val rules so truthy/#loop never see a ref)
    95	  rule <k> If(ref(H:Int), T:Stmts, E:Stmts) => If(V, T, E) ... </k>
    96	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    97	       [priority(40)]
    98	  rule <k> IfExp(ref(H:Int), T:Expr, E:Expr) => IfExp(V, T, E) ... </k>
    99	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
   100	       [priority(40)]
   101	  rule <k> ref(H:Int) ~> #whileCond(C:Expr, B:Stmts) => V ~> #whileCond(C, B) ... </k>
   102	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
   103	       [priority(40)]
   104	  // For derefs its iterable ONCE at loop start (iteration is over the snapshot;
   105	  // mutating the iterated list inside its own loop is outside the subset)
   106	  rule <k> For(T:Expr, ref(H:Int), B:Stmts) => For(T, V, B) ... </k>
   107	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
   108	       [priority(40)]
   109	endmodule

     3	module MPY-FUNCTIONS
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	
     6	  // call routing + callee/arg evaluation (#callee/#args/#argCont) live in call.k;
     7	  // this module owns the frame lifecycle (bind params, return, pop).
     8	  syntax KItem ::= frame(continuation: K, callerEnv: Int, savedLoc: Int)
     9	                 | #bindP(ParamNames, Vals)
    10	                 | "#pop"
    11	                 | "#endcall"
    12	
    13	  // ==== def / anonymous closure =============================================
    14	  rule <k> FuncDef(F:String, Params(PNS:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts) => .K ... </k>
    15	       <env> L:Int </env>
    16	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ F <- closureVal(PNS, BODY, L) ], _) ... </scopes>
    17	
    18	  syntax Expr ::= closureExpr(ParamNames, Stmts)
    19	  rule <k> closureExpr(PNS:ParamNames, BODY:Stmts) => closureVal(PNS, BODY, L) ... </k>
    20	       <env> L:Int </env>
    21	
    22	  // ==== annotated def/lambda (closure cells; spec 2.3) ======================
    23	  // closureValC(params, cellvars, body, captured-cells). No frame anchor: all
    24	  // enclosing-local reads are freevars (symtable-complete) and go through the
    25	  // captured cells; everything else is global/builtin, so the callee frame's
    26	  // parent is the module scope (0) — sound after the defining frame dies.
    27	  syntax Val ::= closureValC(ParamNames, ParamNames, Stmts, Map)
    28	
    29	  // capture: resolve each freevar to the enclosing frame's cellRef, then bind
    30	  // (FuncDef) or yield (Lambda) the closure value.
    31	  syntax KItem ::= #mkClosure(String, ParamNames, ParamNames, ParamNames, Stmts, Map)
    32	                 | #mkLambda(ParamNames, ParamNames, ParamNames, Stmts, Map)
    33	  rule <k> FuncDef(F:String, Params(PNS:ParamNames), CellVars(CVS:ParamNames),
    34	                   FreeVars(FVS:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts)
    35	        => #mkClosure(F, PNS, CVS, FVS, BODY, .Map) ... </k>
    36	  rule <k> #mkClosure(F:String, PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames,
    37	                      (FV:String, FVR:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)
    38	        => #mkClosure(F, PNS, CVS, FVR, BODY, CM [ FV <- {M[FV]}:>Val ]) ... </k>
    39	       <env> L:Int </env>
    40	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    41	       requires FV in_keys(M)
    42	  rule <k> #mkClosure(F:String, PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames,
    43	                      .ParamNames, BODY:Stmts, CM:Map) => .K ... </k>
    44	       <env> L:Int </env>
    45	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ F <- closureValC(PNS, CVS, BODY, CM) ], _) ... </scopes>
    46	
    47	  rule <k> Lambda(Params(PNS:ParamNames), E:Expr)
    48	        => closureVal(PNS, Return(E) .Stmts, L) ... </k>
    49	       <env> L:Int </env>
    50	  rule <k> Lambda(Params(PNS:ParamNames), CellVars(CVS:ParamNames),
    51	                  FreeVars(FVS:ParamNames), E:Expr)
    52	        => #mkLambda(PNS, CVS, FVS, Return(E) .Stmts, .Map) ... </k>
    53	  rule <k> #mkLambda(PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames,
    54	                     (FV:String, FVR:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)
    55	        => #mkLambda(PNS, CVS, FVR, BODY, CM [ FV <- {M[FV]}:>Val ]) ... </k>
    56	       <env> L:Int </env>
    57	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    58	       requires FV in_keys(M)
    59	  rule <k> #mkLambda(PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames, .ParamNames, BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)
    60	        => closureValC(PNS, CVS, BODY, CM) ... </k>
    61	
    62	  // ==== bind params ========================================================
    63	  rule <k> #bindP(.ParamNames, .Vals) => .K ... </k>
    64	  rule <k> #bindP((P:String, PS:ParamNames), (V:Val, VS:Vals)) => #bindP(PS, VS) ... </k>
    65	       <env> L:Int </env>
    66	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ P <- V ], _) ... </scopes>
    67	  // a param that is a cellvar was pre-bound to its cell at frame entry
    68	  rule <k> #bindP((P:String, PS:ParamNames), (V:Val, VS:Vals))
    69	        => #cellW({M[P]}:>Val, V) ~> #bindP(PS, VS) ... </k>
    70	       <env> L:Int </env>
    71	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    72	       requires "$cells" in_keys(M)
    73	        andBool pnMember(P, cellsOf({M["$cells"]}:>Val))
    74	        andBool P in_keys(M) andBool isCellRef({M[P]}:>Val)
    75	       [priority(40)]
    76	
    77	  // ==== return / pop the frame (the returned expr evaluates by strictness) ==
    78	  rule <k> Return(V:Val) ~> _ => #pop </k>
    79	       <ret> noRet => retV(V) </ret>
    80	  rule <k> #endcall => #pop ... </k>
    81	       <ret> noRet => retV(noneV) </ret>
    82	  // pop: restore env, DEALLOCATE the callee frame, and wind scopeLoc back (LIFO allocation
    83	  // makes the saved loc the callee frame's own loc). Sound because no closureVal outlives its
    84	  // defining frame (frontend subset: no returned/stored closures; module defs live in loc 0).
    85	  rule <k> #pop => V ~> CONT </k>
    86	       <ret>   retV(V) => noRet </ret>
    87	       <stack> ListItem(frame(CONT:K, CALLERL:Int, SAVEDL:Int)) => .List ... </stack>
    88	       <env>   L:Int => CALLERL </env>
    89	       <scopes> SC:Map => SC [ L <- undef ] </scopes>
    90	       <scopeLoc> _ => SAVEDL </scopeLoc>
    91	endmodule
     1	// reference/src/semantics/call.k — MPY-CALL
     2	// ONE call route for every callable: evaluate the callee to a VALUE (name lookup reaches
     3	// builtins at the root; a cooled Attribute is a bound method), evaluate the args (the shared
     4	// #evalArgs loop in core.k), then dispatch on the callee value:
     5	//   closureVal    -> bind params, push a frame (user function)
     6	//   boundMethodV  -> applyMethod
     7	//   builtinV      -> the #iterNext folds (sum/all/any/max/min) or applyBuiltin
     8	//   typeV         -> callable type objects: int(...) / str(...)
     9	
    10	module MPY-CALL
    11	  imports MPY-METHODS
    12	  imports MPY-BUILTINS
    13	  imports MPY-FUNCTIONS
    14	
    15	  // a cooled attribute is a bound method value
    16	  rule <k> Attribute(V:Val, M:String) => boundMethodV(V, M) ... </k>
    17	
    18	  // evaluate callee, then args ([owise]: problem-local Call interceptions beat this)
    19	  syntax KItem ::= #callee(Exprs)
    20	  rule <k> Call(Fe:Expr, ARGS:Exprs) => Fe ~> #callee(ARGS) ... </k> [owise]
    21	  rule <k> CV:Val ~> #callee(ARGS:Exprs) => #evalArgs(ARGS, .Vals, toCall(CV)) ... </k>
    22	
    23	  // ==== dispatch on the callee value ========================================
    24	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(OBJ:Val, M:String)), ACC:Vals) => applyMethod(OBJ, M, ACC) ... </k>
    25	
    26	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sum")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #sumAcc(OBJ, 0) ... </k>
    27	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("all")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #allAcc(OBJ)    ... </k>
    28	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("any")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #anyAcc(OBJ)    ... </k>
    29	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("max")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #maxAcc0(OBJ)   ... </k>
    30	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("min")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #minAcc0(OBJ)   ... </k>
    31	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN:String)), ACC:Vals) => applyBuiltin(BN, ACC) ... </k> [owise]
    32	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(typeV(T:String)),     ACC:Vals) => applyBuiltin(T, ACC)  ... </k>
    33	
    34	  // ==== heap-object arguments/receivers =====================================
    35	  // Builtins and type calls READ structure — deref the first two arg positions
    36	  // (covers len/sum/all/any/max/min/sorted/list/set + zip's pair). Mutating list
    37	  // methods take the ref itself; every other method receiver is deref'd.
    38	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN:String)), (ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
    39	        => #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN)), (V, REST)) ... </k>
    40	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    41	       [priority(40)]
    42	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN:String)), (A:Val, ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
    43	        => #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN)), (A, V, REST)) ... </k>
    44	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    45	       requires notBool isRefV(A)
    46	       [priority(40)]
    47	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(typeV(T:String)), (ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
    48	        => #applyK(toCall(typeV(T)), (V, REST)) ... </k>
    49	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    50	       [priority(40)]
    51	
    52	  syntax Bool ::= isMutMethod(String) [function, total]
    53	  rule isMutMethod(M:String)
    54	    => M ==String "append" orBool M ==String "sort" orBool M ==String "extend"
    55	       orBool M ==String "insert" orBool M ==String "pop" orBool M ==String "remove"
    56	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(ref(H:Int), M:String)), ACC:Vals)
    57	        => #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(V, M)), ACC) ... </k>
    58	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    59	       requires notBool isMutMethod(M)
    60	       [priority(40)]
    61	  // non-mutating methods READ their heap-object arguments too (join's list);
    62	  // mutators keep refs (append of a list into a list-of-lists stays aliased)
    63	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(OBJ:Val, M:String)), (ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
    64	        => #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(OBJ, M)), (V, REST)) ... </k>
    65	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    66	       requires notBool isMutMethod(M) andBool notBool isRefV(OBJ)
    67	       [priority(40)]
    68	
    69	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(closureVal(PNS:ParamNames, BODY:Stmts, DEFL:Int)), ACC:Vals) ~> CONT
    70	        => #bindP(PNS, ACC) ~> BODY ~> #endcall </k>
    71	       <env>     CALLERL:Int => NEWL </env>
    72	       <scopes>   STORE:Map => STORE [ NEWL <- scope(.Map, parent(DEFL)) ] </scopes>
    73	       <scopeLoc> NEWL:Int => NEWL +Int 1 </scopeLoc>
    74	       <stack>   .List => ListItem(frame(CONT, CALLERL, NEWL)) ... </stack>

    77	  // parent is the module scope (all enclosing-local reads go through cells),
    78	  // and the cellvars' fresh cells allocate before params bind (a cellvar param
    79	  // then writes through its cell in #bindP).
    80	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(closureValC(PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames, BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)), ACC:Vals) ~> CONT

    82	       <env>     CALLERL:Int => NEWL </env>
    83	       <scopes>   STORE:Map => STORE [ NEWL <- scope(CM [ "$cells" <- cellsMark(CVS) ], parent(0)) ] </scopes>
    84	       <scopeLoc> NEWL:Int => NEWL +Int 1 </scopeLoc>
    85	       <stack>   .List => ListItem(frame(CONT, CALLERL, NEWL)) ... </stack>

    88	  rule <k> #allocCells(.ParamNames) => .K ... </k>
    89	  rule <k> #allocCells((CV:String, R:ParamNames)) => #allocCells(R) ... </k>
    90	       <env> L:Int </env>
    91	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ CV <- cellRef(N) ], _) ... </scopes>
    92	       <heap>    H:Map => (N |-> cellV(noneV)) H </heap>
    93	       <heapLoc> N:Int => N +Int 1 </heapLoc>
    94	       requires notBool N in_keys(H)

     2	
     3	module MPY-LIST
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	  imports MPY-ITER
     6	  imports MPY-OPERATORS
     7	
     8	  // ==== iteration (the iterator protocol's list case) =======================
     9	  rule <k> #iterNext(list(.ValSeq))                => #iterDone ... </k>
    10	  rule <k> #iterNext(list(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq))) => #iterYield(V, list(R)) ... </k>
    11	
    12	  // ==== ListExpr: [...] literal -> a fresh heap object =======================
    13	  syntax ApplyK ::= "toList"
    14	  rule <k> ListExpr(ES:Exprs) => #evalArgs(ES, .Vals, toList) ... </k>
    15	  rule <k> #applyK(toList, ACC:Vals) => #alloc(list(vals2valSeq(ACC))) ... </k>
    16	
    17	  // ==== list ops: + / == / != ===============================================
    18	  syntax ValSeq ::= valSeqConcat(ValSeq, ValSeq) [function, total]
    19	  rule valSeqConcat(.ValSeq, T:ValSeq)                => T
    20	  rule valSeqConcat(vCons(V:Val, S:ValSeq), T:ValSeq) => vCons(V, valSeqConcat(S, T))
    21	
    22	  // list + list constructs a NEW object (k-cell — it allocates; operands land here
    23	  // already deref'd). priority(45) beats the generic BinOp dispatch.
    24	  rule <k> BinOp("+", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq)) => #alloc(list(valSeqConcat(A, B))) ... </k>
    25	       [priority(45)]
    26	
    27	  rule applyCmp("==", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq)) => A ==K B
    28	  rule applyCmp("!=", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq)) => notBool (A ==K B)
    29	
    30	  // ==== deep equality when elements are heap objects (list-of-lists) ========
    31	  // Python == is structural at every depth. Fires ONLY when a ref is present
    32	  // (the guard decides on concrete seqs); the plain ==K path above is unchanged.
    33	  syntax Bool ::= hasRefVS(ValSeq) [function, total]
    34	  rule hasRefVS(.ValSeq)                => false
    35	  rule hasRefVS(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq)) => isRefV(V) orBool hasRefVS(R)
    36	
    37	  syntax Bool ::= deepEqVS(ValSeq, ValSeq, Map) [function]
    38	                | deepEqV(Val, Val, Map)        [function]
    39	  rule deepEqVS(.ValSeq, .ValSeq, _:Map)                   => true
    40	  rule deepEqVS(.ValSeq, vCons(_:Val, _:ValSeq), _:Map)    => false
    41	  rule deepEqVS(vCons(_:Val, _:ValSeq), .ValSeq, _:Map)    => false
    42	  rule deepEqVS(vCons(A:Val, As:ValSeq), vCons(B:Val, Bs:ValSeq), HP:Map)
    43	    => deepEqV(A, B, HP) andBool deepEqVS(As, Bs, HP)
    44	
    45	  rule deepEqV(ref(H:Int), B:Val, HP:Map) => deepEqV({HP[H]}:>Val, B, HP)
    46	       requires H in_keys(HP)
    47	  rule deepEqV(A:Val, ref(H:Int), HP:Map) => deepEqV(A, {HP[H]}:>Val, HP)
    48	       requires notBool isRefV(A) andBool H in_keys(HP)
    49	  rule deepEqV(list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq), HP:Map) => deepEqVS(A, B, HP)
    50	  rule deepEqV(A:Val, B:Val, _:Map) => A ==K B [owise]

    58	  syntax KItem ::= #memberAcc(Val, Iterable) | #memberCont(Val) | "#notB"
    59	  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp("in",     list(VS:ValSeq))) => #memberAcc(LV, list(VS)) ... </k>
    60	  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp("not in", list(VS:ValSeq))) => #memberAcc(LV, list(VS)) ~> #notB ... </k>
    61	  rule <k> #memberAcc(V:Val, IT:Iterable) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #memberCont(V) ... </k>
    62	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #memberCont(_V:Val) => false ... </k>
    63	  rule <k> #iterYield(E:Val, _:Iterable) ~> #memberCont(V:Val) => true ... </k>

    65	  rule <k> #iterYield(E:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #memberCont(V:Val) => #memberAcc(V, R) ... </k>

    67	  rule <k> B:Bool ~> #notB => notBool B ... </k>

     5	  imports MPY-ITER

    13	  syntax IntSeq ::= strToCodes(String) [function]
    14	  rule <k> Str(S:String) => str(strToCodes(S)) ... </k>

    17	    requires S =/=String "" andBool ordChar(substrString(S, 0, 1)) <Int 128
    18

    20	  syntax IntSeq ::= seqConcat(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    21	  rule seqConcat(.IntSeq, T:IntSeq)                => T
    22	  rule seqConcat(iCons(I:Int, S:IntSeq), T:IntSeq) => iCons(I, seqConcat(S, T))

    24	  rule applyBin("+",  str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => str(seqConcat(A, B))

    26	  rule applyCmp("!=", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => notBool (A ==K B)
    27	
    28	  // substring membership: `P in X` iff the code-seq P occurs contiguously in X
    29	  rule applyCmp("in",     str(P:IntSeq), str(X:IntSeq)) => strContains(P, X)
    30	  rule applyCmp("not in", str(P:IntSeq), str(X:IntSeq)) => notBool strContains(P, X)

    39	  rule strContains(P:IntSeq, .IntSeq)  => false requires notBool strPrefix(P, .IntSeq)
    40	  rule strContains(P:IntSeq, iCons(C:Int, Xs:IntSeq)) => strContains(P, Xs)
    41	       requires notBool strPrefix(P, iCons(C, Xs))

    48	  syntax Bool ::= strLt(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    49	  rule strLt(.IntSeq, .IntSeq)                => false
    50	  rule strLt(.IntSeq, iCons(_:Int, _:IntSeq)) => true
    51	  rule strLt(iCons(_:Int, _:IntSeq), .IntSeq) => false
    52	  rule strLt(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => true          requires A  <Int B
    53	  rule strLt(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => false         requires A  >Int B
    54	  rule strLt(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => strLt(As, Bs) requires A ==Int B

    57	  rule applyCmp(">",  str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => strLt(B, A)
    58	  rule applyCmp("<=", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => notBool strLt(B, A)

module MPY-ASSERT
  imports MPY-CORE

  rule <k> Assert(V:Val) => .K ... </k>
       requires truthy(V)
  rule <k> Assert(V:Val) ~> _ => .K </k>
       <exc> NoExc => AssertionError </exc>
       <exit-code> _ => 1 </exit-code>
       requires notBool truthy(V)

  rule <k> Assert(ref(H:Int)) => Assert(V) ... </k>
       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
       [priority(40)]
